item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.9.10, build 2477

The planar tracker

  • The PlanarTracker's panel is rebuilt to its design. The Track tab has operation (Track or Steady), the reference frame with Set and Go, then Pattern and Tracking. Surface holds the plane's corners, and Output the tracked corners with Create pin.
  • Pattern:
    • track outside the shape;
    • an occlusion matte from any node in the comp, its alpha or red, so a hand passing in front is left out;
    • five motion toggles (translate, scale, rotate, shear, perspective) that make the motion model;
    • channel, and adapt to light changes.
  • tracker: Hybrid is new. After the features are fitted, every pixel of the plane lines it up with the reference frame. It lands closer (ten times closer on our test plates), follows a change of light, and carries the plane on through frames where too few features are left.
  • Tracking:
    • Analyze, and step or run a frame at a time, either way;
    • trim the keys before, after, at this frame or between keys;
    • search area; share, refine and smooth;
    • a confidence for every frame, with mark below and stop when below.
  • Steady holds the plane still where it is at the reference frame, so any drift in the track shows as the plane moving.
  • In the Viewer, the tracked plane draws with a grid and short trails behind its corners. The features used show green and those left out red, with their counts. A track bar sits under the Viewer's bars: step buttons, the motion toggles, search, Steady, Refine and Export.
  • A Confidence strip under the Viewer runs along the shot. The frames under mark below are shaded and the run at the playhead is named ("1005 to 1007 low"). Click in it to go to a frame.
  • Refine opens the four corners magnified. This frame's are on top; under each is the reference frame, or the frame before, carried by the track. Drag in a loupe to nudge its corner, blended over a few frames either side. Nudges are kept when you track again. Previous low frame and Next low frame step through the weak frames.
  • Export makes nodes from the track:
    • a Planar Transform, live or baked;
    • a corner pin, relative or absolute;
    • a stabilize or a match-move;
    • a Tracker with a track at each corner, for Nuke.
    The matrix, Roto, mesh and 3D items are on the menu, dim, and say what's missing.
  • Not in Kento yet, shown dim: tracking a Roto layer, point tracks to help the plane, max motion, Stop and Track between keys, motion blur, a lens, and the panel's Corner pin, Stabilize and Match-move operations (use Export).

Remote control

  • planar.track steps or runs from one frame to another. planar.trim, planar.nudge and planar.export are new.

The manual

  • The tracking chapter covers the planar tracker.
  • Seven new diagrams: a comp's files, the Text row, the Settings window, the Shortcuts keyboard, a kernel's parts, the Shot panel, and how a projection works, seen from above.

Kento Alpha 0.9.9, build 2466

Properties' size

  • Settings > Preferences > Interface > Sizes has Properties beside Node Graph: a slider from 80 to 160%, notched at 90, 100, 120 and 140%. It sizes Properties' panels whole, their words, fields, sliders, buttons and rows, and the menus they open. Open panels are made again at the new size, and the Properties pane widens to fit.
  • Under the sliders, three nodes are drawn at 100% beside the Node Graph size you chose, and change as you drag.
  • The Viewer, the Node Graph and the other panels keep their size.
  • A few parts of Kento's own tools' panels that are drawn their own way stay at 100% for now.

Kento's own nodes' panels

  • Menus read in words: WhiteBalance's shades of gray, Linearise's sRGB, BT.1886 and BT.2446 Method A (to HDR).
  • Measured readings (Cambi's score, WhiteBalance's estimate and gain, Deflicker's frame mean) show whole instead of cut in the middle.
  • Deband's and AutoDeband's direction reads in degrees, -360 to 360.
  • The Generative nodes' first tab is named for the node (Halation, Generate), as Kento's own nodes' are.
  • Frame Repair has Add this frame and Remove this frame under its bad frames.
  • Layer Mux's Layers section says where its rows come from before anything is plugged in; Layer Filter's layers line and Prerender's notes show whole.
  • Every Generative node and every node of Kento's own now has a Help tab: what it's for, how to use it, and what to watch for.

Roto

  • The selected shape's colour is a color row as Grade's is: one value on a slider for all four channels, the swatch opening the color picker, and 4 splitting it into red, green, blue and alpha. It was four numbers in a text box.
  • Opacity, feather, falloff, colour, shutter and blending each have a key diamond at the end of the row: click it to key that setting at this frame, so it changes over time; click a filled one to take the key off.

Gizmos as Bentos

  • A gizmo you import (File > Import > Gizmo..., or a .gizmo dropped on the Node Graph) becomes a Bento: it's published to your first Bento library under Gizmos, and the node is that Bento, with its tile, its controls and Edit inside. The same file again uses the same Bento; a changed file is its next version.
  • It keeps the gizmo's class: a .nk or .ko saves it as the gizmo's own node with the controls you changed, so Nuke opens it as before.
  • Opening a comp that uses a gizmo already in your library brings its nodes in as that Bento, unless a control of theirs is animated or driven by an expression. A gizmo that rebuilds itself when a control changes stays a group.

X-spline shapes

  • Roto and RotoPaint have a new shape, the X-spline (Shift+K, beside B-spline): click its points and it curves smoothly through them. Each point has a tension on the Roto tab: -1 smooth through the point, 0 a sharp corner, 1 rounded off near it, so one shape mixes smooth, sharp and soft corners with no tangents to pull.
  • Convert to turns a Bezier or B-spline into an X-spline and back. A .nk writes it as the B-spline of its points; a .ko keeps it.

Kento Alpha 0.9.8, build 2451

The color picker

  • Every color swatch opens Kento's own color picker: a square of saturation and value beside a hue strip, drawn as your display shows them.
  • RGB (with alpha, where the color has one) and HSV are linear values, as the comp works in them, and can go past 1. The menu at the end of the hex row shows them in another of the config's spaces; the knob always gets the working space.
  • hex is the color as the display shows it; type a code to set it.
  • Pick from the Viewer: a point, or the average of an area you drag, of the picture coming into the node (before) or the one it makes (after).
  • Screen... opens the system's color window, to pick from anywhere on the screen.
  • recent keeps the last six colors you chose; swatches are your own (+ adds one, right-click removes it). Both are kept with your preferences.

The Viewer

  • The input process works, as in Nuke: name any image node VIEWER_INPUT (a grade, a group) and the Viewer shows its picture through it, for the eye only. IP on bar 1 turns it off and on. The pixel readout and the scopes read the picture itself. A .nk keeps a Viewer's IP turned off and another node's name.

Motion

  • The Motion window's Edit works: the motion as Nuke's expression, to change as you like; Apply writes it onto the knobs, curve standing for the knob's own keys.
  • Each setting of a motion (amplitude, frequency, roughness...) can be linked to another knob with the link button at the end of its row: the motion follows that knob, live, and a bake keeps its values.

The Node Graph

  • ⌥H (Edit > Node > Hide input) hides a node's input wire, leaving a short stub at the input; it shows dashed while the node or its source is selected. The Node tab's hide input does the same, and a .nk's hide input comes in and goes back.
  • ⌘F7 to ⌘F10 keep the Node Graph's view, zoom and group; ⇧F8 to ⇧F10 go back to them (the first from Edit > Node Graph location).
  • ⇧⌘B bookmarks the selected nodes.
  • ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ (Edit > Node > Version up and down) step the selected Reads to their next or previous version on disk, and Writes one version on or back.

Tracking

  • A track handed over shows the point it lost in a dashed box, "lost at" its frame, and, selected, a card saying when it was handed over and the offset kept.

Roto

  • Per-point feather, under Selected shape on the Roto tab: how far the point picked in the Viewer has its feather point, in pixels. Change it and the feather moves along the way it stands out, or straight out from the shape for a point with no feather yet.
  • The Dope Sheet opens a Roto or RotoPaint into its shapes and strokes, each with its tool's icon and its lifetime as a bar in its color: drag an end to change that frame, or the bar to slide it. This frame keeps only what's drawn at the current frame.
  • Freehand (⇧V) draws a shape by hand: drag round the outline and it becomes a smooth Bezier.

Report a problem

  • A report filed in the studio bug tracker now takes its .zip with it (the comp, every picture, the voice note), up to 100 MB; a bigger one stays on your Mac and the note says so.
  • Help > My reports shows how each filed report stands in the tracker: Open, In progress, Resolved or Won't fix, with the pipeline team's reply under it.

The look

  • Each pane's menu (split, float, its panels) is a small icon at the end of its tab row, where a blank square was. The Viewers panel, alone in its pane, shows one row: its strip, with the same icon.
  • One error red everywhere: a node's error glow and the error card use the same red.
  • The transport's buttons are outlines: bars and triangles at the ends, a chevron a frame either way.
  • A Read's Colour tab says what its file tells of its color: file type, bit depth, what the file says, the rules that match, every guess, and what it's read as.

Fixes

  • The Dope Sheet's rows follow an undo at once (a shape's keys moved back showed where they had been).
  • The Timeline under the Viewer is never cut off: in a narrow window its transport line shows in full below the ruler, and so does its sound lane.

Color

  • A Nuke script saved back from Kento writes the kinds you chose in This comp > Colour > Reading files by kind as its Project Settings' LUTs.

The manual

  • Every guide chapter now starts with a Try it; the keyboard shortcuts chapter's shows how to look a key up and give a free key an action.
  • The getting-started chapters have them too: make room for the picture and put the window back, save and version up a comp, find a key and a node's help. Getting help's page on reporting a problem now matches the window.
